answer: Producing a novel, coherent answer each epoch is cheap per alias but prohibitive across thousands, so scale buys less credibility — the attacker cannot simply buy a large, credible flock. It survives because reputation is spent fast and earned slowly, so any alias that ever cheats loses value that is expensive to replace. The practical upshot is that honesty is the only strategy that scales — a farm that tries to game the system pays for each identity it adds. Consider a voyage as the anchor of the cost.
